title: Multifactor authentication for email
question: Must each work email account use a second proof of who you are, as well as a password?
why: It helps protect email if a password is stolen.

title: Email filtering and forwarding
question: Does your email service block spam and harmful software, and stop auto-forwarding to outside addresses?
explanation: Auto-forwarding sends a copy of mail to another address.
why: These checks help block harmful mail and stop copies going outside the clinic.

title: Antivirus protection
question: Do all computers have virus or threat protection that updates itself?
explanation: This software helps spot and block harmful activity on a computer.
why: Up-to-date protection helps detect threats on work computers.

title: Automatic updates
question: Do operating systems and web browsers install updates on their own?
explanation: The operating system is the main software that runs a device.
why: Updates fix weak spots that attackers could use.

title: Portable device encryption
question: Is stored data encrypted on every laptop, tablet and phone that can access patient data?
explanation: Encryption scrambles data. A key or login is needed to read it.
why: It helps protect data if a device is lost or stolen.

title: Individual accounts
question: Does each staff member have their own login, with no shared accounts?
why: Separate logins help control access and show who did what.

title: Multifactor authentication for clinical systems
question: Must your patient record, billing, telehealth and remote access systems each use a second proof of identity as well as a password?
explanation: This is called multifactor authentication. Telehealth is care by phone or video. Remote access links to a work system from another place.
why: A stolen password should not be enough to get into systems that hold patient data. Check all of them.

title: Removing access when staff leave
question: When a staff member leaves, are all their work accounts turned off that same day?
why: Former staff should no longer have access to work systems or patient data.

title: Limiting administrator rights
question: Are admin rights given only to people who need them for their role?
explanation: Admin rights let a person change key system settings.
why: This limits who can make large changes or gain broad access.

title: Daily separated backups
question: Are backups made at least daily and kept offline or in a separate account that an attack on work systems could not reach?
explanation: A backup is a copy used to get lost data back.
why: Protected copies help you recover after an attack, failure or loss.

title: Testing backup recovery
question: In the last six months, has someone restored a file from backup to check that it works?
explanation: Restore means get a file back from a saved copy.
why: A backup is useful only if you can get data back when needed.

title: Vendor agreements
question: Do you have a signed Business Associate Agreement with each vendor that needs one because it handles patient data for you?
explanation: This is a contract that sets out the vendor's duties to protect patient data.
why: It helps make clear how the vendor protects data and deals with problems.

title: Secure disposal
question: Are old computers, phones and drives wiped so data cannot be read, or destroyed, before they leave the clinic?
explanation: Wiping removes stored data so others cannot get it back.
why: Deleting a file may leave its data on the drive. Someone else may still read it.

title: Updated inventory
question: Do you have a written list of devices and software that can access patient data, checked and updated in the last year?
explanation: The list you make for ClinicShield can help.
why: You need to know what you own to protect it and spot what is missing.

title: Separate guest Wi-Fi
question: Is guest or patient Wi-Fi separate from the network used by work computers?
why: This helps stop visitor devices from reaching work systems.

title: Router security
question: Has the router or firewall's default admin password been changed, and has its firmware been updated in the last year?
explanation: Firmware is software built into a device. A default password is one set by the vendor.
why: Old software and default passwords can leave a way in for attackers.

title: Protected remote access
question: Is remote access to clinic computers off unless needed, and does each link that stays on require a second proof of identity as well as a password?
explanation: This is multifactor authentication. If all remote access is off, answer Yes. If any active link lacks this extra login check, answer No. If not checked, choose Unknown. A virtual private network (VPN) alone is not enough.
why: Open remote access can give attackers a way into work systems.

title: Supported operating systems
question: Does every device still get security fixes for its operating system, through normal or valid extended support?
explanation: This is the main software that runs the device. Examples are Windows and macOS.
why: When support ends, the vendor may no longer fix weak spots.

title: Checking installed updates
question: Does someone check at least monthly that updates were installed on every machine?
why: Auto-updates can fail. Check that each device got the fixes it needs.

title: Written incident plan
question: Do you have a short written plan for whom to call and what to do if ransomware hits or a laptop goes missing?
explanation: Ransomware is an attack that locks or steals data and demands payment.
why: A plan helps staff act fast and work together to recover.

title: Reporting security problems
question: Does everyone know how to report a suspicious email or a lost device, and whom to contact?
why: Early reports give the clinic more time to limit harm and protect data.

title: Breach notification preparation
question: Do you know who must be told, and by when, if patient data is breached?
explanation: A breach can mean data was exposed or used without permission.
why: A clear contact and notice process helps avoid missed steps or deadlines.

title: Medical device inventory and separation
question: Are medical devices on the network listed with their vendor support status and kept on a separate network where possible?
explanation: These can include imaging tools, monitors and dental sensors.
why: Devices can be hard to update. Check their support and limit who can reach them.

title: Security responsibility and risk analysis
question: Think about security, even if it is a part-time role. Is one person named to lead it, and is a risk analysis from the last 12 months complete and written down?
explanation: A risk analysis checks how patient data could be exposed or lost and what safeguards are needed.
why: Clear roles and a written check help staff find risks. They also help staff act on fixes.

title: Staff security training
question: Does each staff member get security awareness training when hired and at least once a year?
why: Training helps staff spot threats and follow safe work steps.
